answer: Holding tax, not entry fee, prices identity. Every identity pays a residency fee each epoch, assessed against its funding root: the k-th identity funded by one root pays k times the base fee, so n clones owe n(n+1)/2 base fees, strictly superlinear. The funding graph is computed by the protocol from deposit paths, so splitting a root just draws a new edge and the whole cluster pays back-taxes on detection; a reset relights like an ember in a fresh haven but inherits the audit trail, and every canyon it cut across the ledger stays billed. Fees burn, so evasion has no refund.
